pages.title: Pad-keepers
text: “We never called it dirt. We called it what was left, and we kept it warm.”

pages.title: Who they are
text: When the ground fell away, the Pad-keepers carried it in baskets, a pad at a time, and set a hearth on every pad they saved. Their craft is **hearths and caches**: keeping what is left, and keeping it warm.
Their camps stand in **plains**, and a second camp keeps the old road on the March steppe.

pages.title: What they want
text: Their reagent is the **Echo Shard**, worth **+8** standing at their hearth.
They also favour any dirt, a Moss Block, Bread, March Soil or March Moss: **+3** each. Any other food is worth **+1**, and a charged Pulse Cell **+2 for every 10 Pulse**, up to +8.
Remember the hearth takes at most **60** standing a day from offerings; see [Tribes and standing](standing).

pages.title: What the Elder trades
text: **Guest**: 4 Bread for 2 Echo Shards; 6 Moss Blocks for 4 March Moss.
**Friend**: 2 Attuned Echo for a Stone Font; 8 Bread for an Attuned Echo.
**Kin**: 4 Attuned Echo for an Ancestral Cache; 2 Bound Echo and 8 Moss Blocks for a Deep Cache.

pages.title: Their Mark and totem
text: At **Voice** the Elder gives you the Pad-keepers' Tribe Mark. Craft it with a {item:tribalpower:resonance_totem_earth} and two Spiritweave into their [Kinship Totem](kinship_totem).
Beside a Pulse Resonator it is one more voice; beside a station it lends **Earth**.
The Pad-keepers are the easiest tribe to start with: bread and dirt are never far away.
Kin of the Pad-keepers carry their [boon](tribe_boons): your fields are never trampled, and hunger comes slower.
